[F003] The fix is verified — the auditor's isolated reproduction now returns `has_block: False` with zero flags.

**[high, correctness] `plan-review` falsely flags `dontpanic plan-review` as a block-severity `missing_prereq`** — Addressed. Root cause: `extract_named_tokens` correctly extracts the full invocation phrase `dontpanic plan-review` as a command, but `Resolvers.resolves_command` only did exact-membership against bare subcommand names, and the real `build_default_resolvers()` populates `commands` solely from `command_validation.known_subcommands()` (which lists `plan-review`, never `dontpanic plan-review`). The lint test had masked this by hand-stuffing `"dontpanic"` and full phrases into its resolver set, but production resolvers don't. I normalized CLI invocation prefixes in `Resolvers.resolves_command` (`scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/plan_review/lint.py`): it now (1) keeps the exact-phrase match, then (2) strips a leading CLI-binary token (new `cli_binaries` field defaulting to `{"dontpanic"}`) and resolves on the first remaining word as the subcommand. This accepts the supported `dontpanic <subcommand>` shape and the `quota-caps init` (subcommand + arg) shape while still flagging a genuinely unknown command like `frobnicate widgets` or `dontpanic frobnicate`. The conservative `Resolvers()` default (empty `commands`) still flags everything, so purity/coupling behavior is preserved.

Regression tests added: in `test_plan_review_lint_f001.py` — `test_dontpanic_prefixed_sup
